description: We are a team passionate about data, technology, and space exploration. We aim to use data analysis, software development, and machine learning to explore real-world challenges and transform complex data into meaningful insights and useful solutions. Through the NASA Space Apps Challenge, we hope to learn, collaborate, and build something that can make an impact.
summary:
TerraShift is an interactive climate data visualization platform developed to make long-term temperature changes across South America easier to explore and understand.

Using NASA's MERRA-2 climate dataset, TerraShift analyzes monthly air temperature records from January 2000 to September 2026 across 12 South American countries. The platform features an interactive map displaying estimated warming trends, country-specific historical temperature charts, and tools for comparing temperature changes across the region.

Beyond visualization, TerraShift applies statistical methods, including linear regression and confidence intervals, to estimate temperature trends and communicate the uncertainty associated with those estimates.

The project addresses the challenge of making complex NASA Earth observation data accessible and understandable to a broader audience. Climate datasets are often difficult to interpret without specialized tools or technical knowledge.

By transforming scientific data into clear, interactive visualizations, TerraShift helps students, researchers, and the general public explore regional warming patterns, compare countries, and better understand how temperatures have changed over time.
details:
Project Details — TerraShift

What does TerraShift do?

TerraShift is an interactive web application designed to help people explore and understand long-term temperature changes across South America using NASA Earth observation data.

The platform analyzes monthly near-surface air temperature records from NASA's MERRA-2 dataset, covering January 2000 through September 2026 across 12 South American countries.

Users can interact with a color-coded map to explore estimated warming trends, select individual countries to examine historical temperature records, and compare temperature changes across the region.

For each country, TerraShift provides annual average temperature charts, estimated warming rates in degrees Celsius per decade, 95% confidence intervals, and statistical indicators that help users interpret the results.

How does it work?

TerraShift processes historical temperature data obtained through NASA Giovanni and MERRA-2. The application organizes monthly observations by country and calculates annual averages using complete calendar years.

Linear regression is used to estimate long-term temperature trends. The application also implements Newey–West heteroskedasticity and autocorrelation-consistent (HAC) standard errors to provide uncertainty estimates that account for potential temporal dependence.

The results are presented through an interactive dashboard, allowing users to explore climate patterns without needing to write code or perform statistical calculations themselves.

Tools and technologies

TerraShift was developed using:

  • Python: Data processing, statistical analysis, and application development.
  • Streamlit: Interactive web dashboard and user interface.
  • Pandas and NumPy: Data preparation and numerical computations.
  • Statistical modeling libraries: Linear regression, confidence intervals, and diagnostic analysis.
  • NASA MERRA-2 and Giovanni: Historical climate data and data access.
  • GeoJSON and interactive mapping: Geographic visualization of South American countries.
  • Git and GitHub: Version control and source code management.
  • Streamlit Community Cloud: Public application deployment.

What makes TerraShift creative?

TerraShift combines geographic visualization, historical climate analysis, and statistical uncertainty into a single accessible platform.

Rather than simply displaying temperature measurements, it helps users understand how temperatures have changed over time and how confidently those trends can be estimated.

Its interactive map makes it possible to compare countries visually, while its detailed statistical views provide additional context for users interested in the underlying evidence.

The platform also distinguishes between complete and incomplete years, preventing partial annual observations from being treated as full-year averages.

Benefits and intended impact

Climate data is publicly available, but interpreting large scientific datasets can be challenging for people without specialized technical knowledge.

TerraShift aims to reduce that barrier by transforming NASA climate records into clear, interactive, and understandable visualizations.

The platform can support students, educators, researchers, and anyone interested in exploring historical temperature changes across South America.

By making regional climate information easier to access and interpret, TerraShift encourages scientific curiosity, climate awareness, and evidence-based discussions about environmental change.

Development considerations and limitations

Scientific transparency and reproducibility were important considerations throughout development.

TerraShift communicates statistical uncertainty through confidence intervals and diagnostic information. It also distinguishes estimated historical trends from predictions about future climate conditions.

The application uses country-level average temperatures, meaning the map represents differences between national averages rather than temperature variations within each country.

Additionally, the statistical results describe observed historical patterns and should not be interpreted as proof of specific causes or as forecasts of future temperatures.

TerraShift demonstrates how open NASA Earth science data can be transformed into an accessible educational and analytical tool for exploring climate change across South America.
